text:
IncidentsBot: INCIDENT ALERT — p99 latency breach detected for canary deployment 'model-v13-canary' in us-west-2 at 10:12 PDT. Auto-pager sent to on-call. Metrics: p95 740ms, p99 2.8s, streaming stall rate +12%.

Ana Moreno: seeing it on the dashboard. can anyone confirm if this lines up with the v13 traffic shift? :eyes:

Ravi Patel: yep, rollout started at 10:05, 20% traffic to v13. quick snapshot: CPU/GPU utilization looks normal, but we have increased tail latency on mux and a few stalled streaming sessions.

Maya Chen: grabbing logs from edge mux and router. also checking kv-cache eviction spikes.

Jasper Li: i pulled a sampling of streaming sessions — there are repeated "chunk_timeout" entries around the same time as the request spikes. looks like some requests hit a slow path in the decoder kernel.

Lena Park: repeating: is this repeatable on v13 only or also on v12?

Ravi Patel: preliminary: v13 p99 ~2.8s, v12 p99 ~0.95s. so seems canary-specific.

Ana Moreno: okay — mitigation idea: pause traffic to v13 and route canary traffic back to v12 while we triage. can we do a quick rollback toggle?

Oncall Bridge Bot: @Ana Moreno, on-call acknowledged. Paging Jasper, Ravi. Bridge created: https://redwood/bridge/5175001111

Jasper Li: i'm on it. preparing rollback command.

Ravi Patel: FYI logs show kv-cache churn: eviction rate doubled after v13 instances started, might be a quantization-induced longer kernel cold path causing KV cache pressure.

Maya Chen: grabbing kernel traces now. also instrumenting streaming mux to dump per-connection stalls.

Ana Moreno: perform rollback only if safe. confirm graceful draining so in-flight streams don't get killed. How long to toggle?

Jasper Li: toggle should be sub-2min for routing change. drain window set to 60s. rolling back to v12 via internal API:

```
# internal rollout control
POST /internal/rollouts/update
{
  "deployment": "model-v13-canary",
  "action": "set_traffic",
  "split": {"model-v12": 1.0, "model-v13": 0.0},
  "drain_seconds": 60
}
```

Jasper Li: executing now.

IncidentsBot: ACTION LOG — rollback command issued by Jasper Li at 10:18 PDT.

Maya Chen: kernel traces show a lock contention hotspot in the new decoder kernel under longer sequence lengths — seems to disproportionally affect streaming sessions that are mid-conversation (long KV lookups).

Ravi Patel: posted a short patch that adds a per-request timeout fallback on the decoder path. not going to prod this fast; we need root cause and maybe adjust quantization profile.

Ana Moreno: customer impact check — which tenants are affected? any high-SLAs in the affected region?

Ravi Patel: cross-referencing usage: 3 enterprise customers had elevated errors in us-west-2 during the window. latency not leading to errors in most cases, but we saw degraded streaming quality (gaps) for some voice/streaming integrations.

Lena Park: opened a customer-impact ticket and pinged CSMs for the 3 accounts. #support has the ticket id: SUP-3312.

Oncall Bridge Bot: Bridge note: rollback completed at 10:20 PDT, traffic now 100% v12. Observed p95 380ms, p99 0.92s at 10:25. Continuing to monitor.

Maya Chen: after rollback we still see a small bump in eviction rate — likely warmup effects. kv-cache warming should settle in ~10-15min.

Ana Moreno: good. next steps: 1) keep v13 paused, 2) collect full kernel/profile dumps for v13 instances (Jasper + Maya), 3) run load tests with long-conversation streaming to reproduce locally, 4) revisit quantization settings and kernel selection for long sequences.

Jasper Li: exporting full profiler tarball and op trace, uploading to /artifacts/5175001111/profiler.tar.gz. includes decoder traces and per-request histograms.

Ravi Patel: adding a temporary routing policy to avoid sending streaming sessions to canaries until further notice. command: 

```
rctl route update --exclude-tag canary --traffic-type streaming
```

Lena Park: CSMs notified, support ticket updated with mitigation summary. No confirmed data exfiltration or request failures beyond degraded streaming.

Ana Moreno: status update for incident channel: MITIGATED (rollback applied) — impact: elevated p99 and streaming gaps for a small subset of customers in us-west-2 between 10:12–10:20 PDT. root cause: new decoder kernel behavior under v13 quantization leading to lock contention and kv-cache thrash.

Ravi Patel: tagging this for a postmortem. i'll own the RCA with Maya and Jasper. Suggest priority P1-RCA because canary rollouts mustn't cause customer impact.

Maya Chen: scheduling a follow-up deep-dive at 14:00 PDT today. will include reproducer steps and perf diffs.

Oncall Bridge Bot: Handoff: final state — incident mitigated and oncall monitoring. handoff to day-shift team for 14:00 deep-dive. Bridge closed at 10:32 PDT.

Ana Moreno: thanks all. add any lingering notes to the incident doc: https://redwood/incidents/5175001111/doc. :v:
